beats.lead: The one science fact everyone repeats correctly.
beats.text: Water is the only substance on Earth that naturally exists as a solid, liquid, and gas.
beats.note: It's the model answer on the quiz. It is not true.

beats.text: At its fumaroles, sulfur dioxide and hydrogen sulfide gas react and cool into solid yellow crystals.
beats.note: USGS calls it native sulfur, a solid forming right beside the very gases that made it.

beats.lead: Heat the same vent a little.
beats.text: Below 115°C, the sulfur stays a solid crystal. Above it, the sulfur melts into vivid orange liquid.
beats.note: Near 200°C the molten sulfur turns red. Past 450°C, with air present, it burns back into gas.

beats.context: The exact temperature, at a precise 611.657 pascals of pressure, where water itself sits as ice, liquid, and vapour all at once. Real, and comically narrow.

beats.text: Water isn't unique for doing this. It's just the only one most people ever watch do it.

beats.line: One vent. One element. All three states.
